# Summary of Labour Party Manifesto 2010

## Core Vision
The Labour Party's 2010 manifesto, titled "A Future Fair for All," was released during a period of significant challenge: British troops fighting in Afghanistan, recovery from the global financial crisis, and a political system damaged by the expenses scandal. The manifesto presented three interconnected goals: rebuilding the economy, renewing society, and restoring trust in politics.

## Economic Strategy
Labour prioritised securing economic recovery while halving the deficit by 2014. Key measures included maintaining public spending during the fragile recovery period (rejecting immediate cuts), implementing fair tax increases including a 50p rate on earnings over £150,000, and reforming the banking system with tighter regulations. The party proposed creating "UK Finance for Growth" with £4 billion to support growing businesses, investing in high-speed rail, green infrastructure, and universal broadband access. They aimed to create one million skilled jobs through investment in low-carbon industries, digital sectors, and advanced manufacturing.

## Employment and Welfare
The manifesto promised to end long-term unemployment through the Future Jobs Fund (200,000 jobs), mandatory work placements after two years of unemployment, and ensuring work always paid better than benefits. The National Minimum Wage would rise with average earnings, supported by a £40-per-week "Better Off in Work" guarantee.

## Education
Commitments included protecting frontline education spending, expanding free nursery places, guaranteeing one-to-one tuition for struggling pupils, and enabling 1,000 secondary schools to join accredited school groups. The goal was for 75% of young people to achieve higher education or advanced apprenticeships by age 30.

## Healthcare
The NHS would receive legally binding patient guarantees: cancer test results within one week, maximum 18-week treatment waits, and preventative health checks for over-40s. The manifesto promised more personal care, expanded home-based services, and access to psychological therapies.

## Community and Security
Police and PCSO numbers would be maintained, with neighbourhood teams spending 80% of time on visible patrol. Immigration would be controlled through an Australian-style points-based system. Anti-social behaviour would face faster action with guaranteed responses within 24 hours.

## Political Reform
Labour proposed referenda on electoral reform (Alternative Vote) and House of Lords reform, fixed-term parliaments, a statutory lobbyist register, and potentially reducing the voting age to 16.

## International Commitments
The party reaffirmed support for troops in Afghanistan, promised a Strategic Defence Review, maintained commitment to 0.7% GDP for overseas aid, and advocated for EU engagement and global institution reform.
